name: Xi'an Street Emotions for Visitors: Six Scales from 0 to 100
description:
Method replication: participants rate 20 Xi'an street views on six emotion dimensions (beautiful, boring, depressing, lively, safe, wealthy) with sliders from 0 to 100, after saying whether they are a visitor or a resident; the images are not the paper's stimuli (82 newly fetched Baidu street views inside Xi'an's Third Ring Road, one direction per point, cropped to remove the camera car).

Original study: Qi, Li, Yang & He (2026), Cities 168, 106424. Baidu street views (960 × 640 px, four directions) were taken every 50 m along roads inside Xi'an's Third Ring Road in May 2022. 49 visitors, recruited at tourist sites and screened against the UNWTO definition, scored more than 7,000 images with the Human-Machine Adversarial Scoring Framework: images were shown two at a time, each visitor rated at least 300, one emotion dimension at a time, on a 0–100 scale. A random forest predicted the six emotions for all images and was related to the complexity and coordination of street shapes.

Differences from the original study: (1) one image at a time with all six dimensions together, instead of image pairs rated one dimension at a time; (2) 20 images per participant instead of about 300, and no machine pre-scores; (3) visitor status is asked in one question instead of being checked in person; (4) the end labels "0 = not at all" and "100 = extremely" are written for this template.
author: Qi, Li, Yang & He
